name: geology
source: Tanaka et al. (2014), Geologic Map of Mars, USGS SIM 3292, 1:20M
attribution: USGS Astrogeology / NASA (Tanaka et al. 2014, SIM 3292)
crs_note: lon/lat on the Mars 2000 sphere (R = 3,396,190 m), −180..180 east-positive; split at ±180

properties.description: Relatively smooth plains near the highland/lowland boundary with small knobs and mesas; mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine and possibly volcanic materials.
Rugged, hummocky, pitted plains of poorly defined flows, hundreds to >1,000 km across; interpreted as lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows. Tens of metres or more thick.
Undulating to moderately rugged plains with scattered knobs and mesas of highland material; mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine and other sediments, possibly volcanic rocks.

Planar to undulating plains across most of the northern lowlands; sediments from outflow channels and highland margins, likely with lavas; pervasively modified by periglaciation and mantling. Hundreds of metres to km thick.
Planar flood lavas with lobate scarps, sinuous troughs and platy textures; largely unmodified flows from fissures and shields. Metres to tens of metres thick.
Hummocky to undulating, internally stratified deposits; interpreted as ice-rich loess modified by periglacial processes (thumbprint terrain, pedestal craters). Tens of metres thick.
Rugged, hummocky, pitted plains of poorly defined flows, hundreds to >1,000 km across; interpreted as lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows. Tens of metres or more thick.
